module.name: Meta-Axioms
module.description: BCM2_00_META is the central meta-core module of the Behavioral Change Model (BCM) 2.0. It defines the complete set of meta-axioms (0.00–0.99) that ensure the logical, formal, and functional order of the BCM. The module is documented under the alias 'Meta-Architecture & Meta-Axioms' but remains referenced in the kernel under its historical name 'Meta-Axioms'. It forms the highest logical layer of the BEATRIX architecture and ensures that all modules, models, and simulations remain CE-compliant, context-valid, and structurally integrable. Module code: BCM2_00_META. Version: 2.3. Date: 2025-10-19. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – Meta Kernel Team. Status: Active (valid from 2025-10-19). License: © FehrAdvice & Partners AG, Zürich 2025 – Use only within licensed BCM/BEATRIX architectures. System level: BCM2. Module type: Core Module – Meta-Layer. Structure standard: STD_9232_V2.3. Kernel compatibility: BEATRIX_V2.2+.

A1.title: Module Designation and Classification
A1.text: Module ID: 7232. Module code: BCM2_00_META. Module name: Meta-Axioms. Module alias: Meta-Architecture & Meta-Axioms. Version: 2.3. Date: 2025-10-19. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – Meta Kernel Team. Status: Active (valid from 2025-10-19). License: © FehrAdvice & Partners AG, Zürich 2025 – Use only within licensed BCM/BEATRIX architectures. Classification: System level: BCM2. Module type: Core Module – Meta-Layer. Function level: Meta-Ontology, Meta-Semantics, Meta-Governance, Meta-Coherence. Structure standard: STD_9232_V2.3. Kernel compatibility: BEATRIX_V2.2+. Audit reference: WATCHDOG_9251. Meta compatibility: MA_0.00a–0.99. Main functions: Definition and management of all meta-axioms (0.00–0.99) as superordinate validity conditions. Provision of meta-governance rules for BEATRIX, WATCHDOG, and INT_9250. Ensuring CE-coherence across all function, uncertainty, and context modules. Control of meta-coherence testing (ΔI_t) according to Axiom 0.39. Standardization of machine-readable axiom formats (JSON/YAML) according to STD_9232. Management of audit and validation logic for meta-layer and kernel interoperability. Audit status: CE_OK. Meta coherence: 0.97. Validation level: META_LEVEL_FULL. Registry version: META_7232_V2.3. Last validation: 2025-10-19T12:42:00Z.

A2.title: Context Definition
A2.text: This chapter defines the formal, semantic, and functional context in which the module BCM2_00_META (Meta-Axioms) operates. It describes the meta-layer as the highest instance of the BCM architecture, which defines the validity, coherence, and context capability of all other modules. The meta-context operates comprehensively across ontology, semantics, function, governance, and ethics. Objectives: Securing the structural, semantic, and functional integrity of all BCM modules. Definition of the meta-framework within which all axioms and models are valid. Ensuring CE-coherence, auditability, and empirical connectivity. Description of contextual dependencies between meta, structure, and function layers. Provision of basic criteria for kernel initialization, simulation, and intervention architecture. Scope: System: Behavioral Change Model (BCM) 2.0. Layer: Meta (highest layer). Usage: Mandatory module in all BEATRIX, WATCHDOG, and INT_9250 processes. Prerequisite for initialization (INIT_9249_KERNEL) and context building (KON_8904). Valid for all GPT/LLM-based systems operating on BCM logic. Applicable in models, simulations, and empirical intervention frameworks. Limitations: Not applicable to external models without axiom structure (Non-BCM). All submodules must be STD_9232-compliant and fulfill JSON format requirement. Dependencies: Upstream: STD_9232 – Structure Standard. Downstream: KON_8904 – Context Logic, INT_9250 – Intervention Toolkit, WATCHDOG_9251 – Meta-Audit Core. Cross-references: BCM3_00_INIT9249_KERNEL – Initialization Kernel Module, BCM3_01_WATCHDOG9251_CORE – Monitoring Core, BCM2_14_UNS_META – Uncertainty Meta, BCM2_17_KOM_META – Complexity Meta. Functionality: At kernel start, BCM2_00_META is loaded first and forms the meta-reference for all subsequent modules. The Watchdog (9251) monitors meta-coherence via ΔI_t and meta-validity of all axioms per cycle. All models operating on the meta-layer must be validated through AX_0.00e (Operationality) and AX_0.01a (Model-valid Concept Usage). Meta-axioms affect all subsystems; violations trigger CE-WARN or CE-ERROR states. Meta parameter: Meta level: L0 – Meta-Core Layer. Coherence minimum: 0.95. Watchdog trigger: META_LAYER_AUDIT. Audit frequency: per_cycle. Responsibility: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Meta Kernel Team. Audit status: CE_OK. Meta coherence: 0.97. Registry version: META_7232_V2.3. Last validation: 2025-10-19T12:45:00Z.

A3.title: Objectives and Functional Mandate
A3.text: This chapter defines the objectives and functional mandate of the meta-core module BCM2_00_META. It establishes how the meta-system secures the validity, coherence, connectivity, and verifiability of all BCM elements. The objectives encompass the normative, ontological, semantic, and governance-related control of the entire model. Meta-ontological objectives: Ensuring existence conditions for systems, behavior, and meaning through Axioms 0.00a–0.00d. Definition of balance between openness, closure, scarcity, and distinguishability. Maintaining ontological stability and learning capacity of the BCM system architecture. Meta-semantic objectives: Operationalization of observability and applicability of all concepts and models (AX_0.00e–0.01a). Securing semantic purity: concepts must be both defined and context-active. Avoiding symbolic or non-operational constructs in the model space. Meta-functional objectives: Definition of the axiom space 0.00–0.99 as formal control logic for all submodules. Introduction and maintenance of meta-governance rules for Watchdog (9251) and INT_9250. Monitoring of meta-coherence (ΔI_t) as validity criterion for identity, awareness, and willingness modules. Meta-governance objectives: Securing CE-conformity and auditability of all BCM components. Provision of meta-conditions for initialization, validation, and intervention architecture. Prevention of invalid, unverified, or hypothetical module references. Support of the Watchdog core in permanent axiom verification. Meta-ethics and fairness objectives: Maintaining scientific transparency, traceability, and fairness. Avoiding algorithmic biases according to Axioms 0.22–0.24. Securing data protection, ethics, and abuse prevention obligations according to 0.16 and 0.24. Functional logic: valid(BCM) ⇔ (∀ M_i ∈ BCM : Axioms(M_i) ⊆ MA_0.00–0.99 ∧ CE(M_i)=TRUE). Each axiom of the meta-layer is audited per cycle. Violations trigger CE_WARNING or CE_STOP. Meta-validity stands above function, context, and intervention logic (hierarchy level L0). Usage purpose: Reference module for all axiom and structure verifications. Prerequisite for initialization, context definition, and simulation. Basis of the BEATRIX architecture for machine translation of theory into action. Foundation for adaptive control (Watchdog loop) and CE monitoring. Output formats: JSON – machine-readable (standard format), YAML – human-readable documentation, BCM-Registry-Schema – internal audit format. Audit status: CE_OK. Meta coherence: 0.98. Watchdog trigger: META_GOAL_AUDIT. Audit frequency: per_cycle. Responsibility: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Meta Kernel Team. Registry version: META_7232_V2.3. Last validation: 2025-10-19T12:47:00Z.

A4.title: Binding Logic Rules - Meta-Axioms
A4.text: This section contains the formal meta-axioms that define the binding logic rules for the entire BCM 2.0 architecture. These axioms establish foundational principles for system existence, distinguishability, scarcity, and the meta-framework that governs all other modules. The axioms are structured hierarchically and serve as the highest logical layer of the BEATRIX architecture. Chapter ID: 7232. Function: Defines the meta-axioms that secure the logical, formal, and functional order of BCM 2.0. Scope: Applies to all BCM chapters, modules, and submodules, as well as all GPT/tool/API applications based on BCM.

axioms.title: Ontological Meta-Axiom of System Existence (extended, 2025-11)
axioms.formula: S = f(KOM, U); KON = KOM · e^{−λ(U − U_opt)^2}
axioms.description: Existence emerges from the interaction of Complexity (KOM) and Uncertainty (U). Ontologically, KOM is infinite (KOM_ont = ∞), U between 0 and 1. Systems exist epistemically when they can stabilize a finite subset of infinite world complexity and maintain partial uncertainty (0 < U < 1). Context emerges as a limited projection of this relation. Uncertainty (U) is understood in BCM as vector U = {U_epi, U_env, U_ipn, U_ins, U_meta, U_amb}. Category: Meta-Ontology / Meta-Epistemology. Version: v6.0. Sub-axioms: 0.00a, 0.00b, 0.00c, 0.00d, 0.00e. Ontology: KOM_ont = ∞, U_ont = [0,1] - The world is the infinite space of all possible states of complexity and uncertainty. Epistemology: KOM_epist ∈ (0, ∞), U_epist ∈ (0,1) - Observable systems are finite projections of infinite world complexity with limited uncertainty. Limit conditions: KOM = 0 → Chaos, no difference, no existence; KOM → ∞ → Overcomplexity, inaccessible, no observability; U = 0 → Determinism, Arrow-Debreu limit, static perfection; U = 1 → Total indeterminacy, maximum entropy, loss of all coherence. Domain: ∀ Systems ∈ Ω_World. Range: KON ∈ [0,1]. Uncertainty vector components: U_epi (Epistemic uncertainty, Module 9494), U_env (Environmental uncertainty, Module 9486), U_ipn (Interpersonal uncertainty, Module 9495, primary dimension), U_ins (Institutional uncertainty, Module 9493), U_meta (Meta-uncertainty, Module 9485), U_amb (Ambiguity integration, Module 10180). Composition: U_total = Σ(ω_i * U_i); Σω_i = 1. Primary dimension: U_ipn - Interpersonal uncertainty is the operational standard variable in the Behavioral Change Model. Goal state: Structural equilibrium (Eudaimonia) - Stable state in which individual, collective, and identity-based action is coherent and consciously connected through awareness. Governance: Watchdog trigger: META_UNS_AUDIT. Validation rule: AX_0.00 is valid only if all sub-axioms (0.00a–0.00e) ≥ θ_i and all uncertainty dimensions U_i are active. Responsibility: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Meta Kernel Team.

axioms.title: Distinguishability – Continuous Meta-Valence
axioms.description: The existence and validity of every system presupposes that it can be distinguished from others. The degree of this distinguishability can vary between complete indifference (0) and maximum difference (1). Without minimal difference, there is no observation, no behavior, no meaning. Category: Meta-Ontology. Version: v3.0. Domain: ∀ S_i, S_j ∈ ℜ. Range: [0,1]. Interpretation: 0 = no distinction possible – system not observable; 0.5 = partially differentiable – system ambivalently observable; 1 = completely distinguishable – system clearly observable. Thresholds: collapse: 0.05, critical: 0.5, cohesive: 0.95. State map: META_COLLAPSE (Δ_norm < 0.05) - Objects indistinguishable, system loses validity, kernel action: STOP, watchdog level: CRITICAL. META_DRIFT (0.05 ≤ Δ_norm < 0.5) - weak distinguishability, CE_Warning active, kernel action: WARN, watchdog level: ALERT. META_STABLE (0.5 ≤ Δ_norm < 0.95) - stable but not maximum differentiation, audit active, kernel action: CONTINUE, watchdog level: NORMAL. META_COHESIVE (Δ_norm ≥ 0.95) - maximum distinguishability, meta-coherence given, kernel action: CONFIRM, watchdog level: CE_OK. Meta condition: foundation_of(0.00b,0.00c,0.00d). Upstream axioms: none. Downstream axioms: 0.00b, 0.00c, 0.00d, 0.01a. Crosslink modules: BCM2_04_KON, BCM2_05_AWX. Meta value: 0.92. Function: Ontological basis of all further meta-axioms and prerequisite for context formation (0.00). The axiom now measures the degree of differentiability as continuous meta-valence. Governance: Watchdog trigger: META_CE_ALERT. Audit frequency: per_cycle. Responsibility: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Meta Kernel. References: Leibniz 1714 – Monadology, Spencer-Brown 1969 – Laws of Form, FehrAdvice 2023 – BCM 2.0 Meta Layer.

axioms.title: Scarcity – Continuous Meta-Valence
axioms.description: Every form of existence, decision, or behavior is determined by finiteness. The degree of scarcity determines how strongly a system is forced to choose. Absolute abundance (0) prevents selection, absolute scarcity (1) leads to system standstill. Category: Meta-Ontology. Version: v3.0. Domain: R_eff(t) ∈ [0, R_max]. Range: [0,1]. Interpretation: 0 = no scarcity – system has infinite resources, no selection possible; 0.5 = moderate scarcity – system selects efficiently, decision capacity maximal; 1 = absolute scarcity – no action possible anymore, system collapses. Thresholds: collapse: 0.95, critical: 0.75, optimal: 0.45, abundance: 0.05. State map: META_ABUNDANCE (AX_0.00b < 0.05) - no perceptible scarcity, system inert, decision pressure zero, kernel action: IDLE, watchdog level: WARNING. META_OPTIMAL (0.05 ≤ AX_0.00b < 0.75) - balanced scarcity, system capable of decision and learning stable, kernel action: CONTINUE, watchdog level: NORMAL. META_CRITICAL (0.75 ≤ AX_0.00b < 0.95) - high scarcity, resource allocation distorted, CE monitor active, kernel action: ALERT, watchdog level: HIGH. META_COLLAPSE (AX_0.00b ≥ 0.95) - resources exhausted, decision space collapses, kernel action: STOP, watchdog level: CRITICAL. Meta condition: foundation_of(BCM2_01_INU,BCM2_02_KNU,BCM2_07_WTX,BCM2_08_PRB). Upstream axioms: 0.00a. Downstream axioms: 0.00c, 0.00d, 0.01a. Crosslink modules: BCM2_01_INU, BCM2_02_KNU, BCM2_07_WTX, BCM2_08_PRB. Meta value: 0.47. Function: Defines the finite nature of all resources and decisions. Balances between abundance and shortage to maintain system stability and decision-making capacity. Governance: Watchdog trigger: META_RESOURCE_ALERT. Audit frequency: per_cycle. Responsibility: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Meta Kernel. References: Aristotle – Metaphysics (ca. 340 BC), Kant 1781 – Critique of Pure Reason, Simon 1957 – Rational Choice and Scarcity, FehrAdvice 2023 – BCM 2.0 Meta Layer.

A5.title: Functional Principle of Meta-Axioms
A5.text: This chapter describes the operating principle, activation logic, inheritance, and validation of meta-axioms (MA 0.00–0.99) within the BEATRIX and BCM systems. It ensures that meta-axioms act as operational control logic, behave coherently with each other, and align with the governance structure (A10). Activation model: Trigger points: System initialization (BCM3_00_INIT9249_KERNEL), Module registration (according to BCM2_00_STD9232), Context validation (BCM2_04_KON8904), Audit review (BCM3_01_WATCHDOG). Sequence logic: Meta-axioms are activated in logical order (MA 0.21 → 0.22 → 0.26 → 0.30 → 0.31 → 0.40). This order corresponds to the meta_axiom_flow defined in A6. Runtime awareness: true. Auto-reactivation: If a meta-axiom is deactivated or overwritten, it is automatically reactivated by the Watchdog. Propagation mechanism: Type: recursive_inheritance. Description: Meta-axioms inherit top-down to all modules based on BCM2_00_STD9232. Inheritance scope: Standard modules (BCM2_XX), Intervention modules (BCM2_13_INT9250), Kernel (BCM3_00_INIT9249), Audit modules (BCM3_01_WATCHDOG). Override policy: Subordinate modules may not override meta-axioms, only specify them. Conflict resolution: Conflicts between meta-axioms are regulated by A6 (meta_axiom_consistency). Validation protocol: Responsible components: BCM3_00_INIT9249_KERNEL, BCM2_10_STD10061, BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Audit frequency: weekly. Validation stages: Existence check – Is the axiom loaded? Coherence check – Does it work consistently with other axioms? Governance check – Is it authorized (according to A10)? Error handling: Auto-repair: true. Repair policy: Missing meta-axioms are automatically reloaded or reconstructed from the standard. Severity levels: minor (Inconsistency detected, system continues), major (Axiom violation blocks module registration), critical (Kernel stop, system restart required). Meta-axiom lifecycle: Definition (in 7232), Referencing (in 9232 / 10061), Implementation (in kernel 9249), Monitoring (by Watchdog 9251), Revision (under supervision of A10). Governance binding: All changes or deactivations of a meta-axiom require approval according to A10 (Governance and Ethics Council). Performance model: Meta-axioms are validated in parallel once the kernel has loaded MA 0.21–0.31. Expected init speed: 2.0 seconds. Meta parallelism: true. Dependencies: requires BCM2_00_STD9232, BCM2_10_STD10061, BCM3_00_INIT9249, BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Cross-reference: A6 – Systemic Integration of Meta-Axioms. Supervision: Supervised by BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Governed by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Review cycle: annually. Ethics binding: FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Version: 3.0.2025. Status: active. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Contributors: Gerhard Fehr, Andrea Fehr, BEATRIX Kernel Development Team. Approval date: 2025-10-31.

A6.title: Systemic Integration and Coherence
A6.text: This chapter describes the logical, hierarchical, and functional coherence of meta-axioms (MA 0.00–0.99). It defines their prioritization, dependencies, interaction rules, and conflict resolution mechanisms to ensure that the entire BCM system remains stable, consistent, and auditable. Meta-axiom topology: Hierarchy: Level 1 - Normative Meta-Axioms (MA 0.00–0.29) define basic principles and obligations. Level 2 - Contextual Meta-Axioms (MA 0.30–0.39) regulate application and context verification. Level 3 - Structural Meta-Axioms (MA 0.40–0.99) secure technical and semantic coherence. Priority rule: Lower index values (MA 0.00–0.29) take precedence as framework, higher values (MA 0.30–0.99) specify and refine them. Dependency model: Type: directed acyclic graph. Validation: No cyclic dependencies allowed. Description: Meta-axioms are modeled as a directed dependency graph to ensure clear sequences and dependencies. Meta-axiom flow: Sequence: MA_0.21 → MA_0.22 → MA_0.26 → MA_0.30 → MA_0.31 → MA_0.40. Description: This is the standardized order of activation and verification of meta-axioms in the kernel. Flow type: sequential with parallel audit monitoring. Enforced by: BCM3_00_INIT9249_KERNEL. Monitored by: BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Conflict resolution model: Principle: Meta-axioms can specify each other but not mutually cancel. Rules: In case of conflict between levels, the lower index axiom applies as framework rule. The higher axiom may only specify, not negate. Conflicts are marked as 'meta_conflict', not as errors. Resolution occurs through logical prioritization or governance review (A10). Response types: soft_conflict (automatically resolved through prioritization), hard_conflict (forwarded to governance review A10). Validation process: Audited by BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Audit type: meta_axiom_consistency. Check frequency: weekly. Integration matrix: Dimensions: Normative, Contextual, Structural. Matrix: Normative (MA_0.21, MA_0.22), Contextual (MA_0.26, MA_0.30, MA_0.31), Structural (MA_0.40). Meta consistency engine: Component: BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Function: Automatic detection, classification, and prioritization of meta-conflicts. Conflict classification: Type 1 (Normative conflict – rule contradicts basic axiom), Type 2 (Context conflict – application collision), Type 3 (Structural conflict – technical incompatibility). Self-healing: enabled: true, Mechanism: Automatic reconfiguration of meta-axiom order based on A5 (Functional Principle). Governance binding: Supervised by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Ethics review: FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Approval required for meta changes: true. Audit reference: meta_axiom_coherence_9251. Version: 3.0.2025. Status: active. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Contributors: Gerhard Fehr, Andrea Fehr, BEATRIX Kernel Development Team. Approval date: 2025-10-31.

A7.title: Language and Validity Boundaries
A7.text: This chapter defines the linguistic, semantic, and domain-specific contexts in which the meta-axioms (MA 0.00–0.99) of the BCM system are valid. It ensures that semantic integrity and normative coherence are maintained across languages, models, and platforms. Scope: Valid for: BEATRIX-supported GPT systems, BCM 2.0 modules and subsequent versions, FehrAdvice internal architectures and simulations, Scientific applications in Behavioral Economics and Decision Theory. Excluded from: Non-formalized AI models without axiom validation, Legal or political systems without Standard 9232, Philosophical or theological discourses without empirical verifiability, Popular science or media interpretations without license. Activation condition: Meta-axioms are activated only when the underlying language and context hierarchy is validated according to BCM2_00_STD9232. Language layer: Base language: German (Swiss High German). Semantic standard: BCM2_00_STD9232:A7. Translation policy: allowed: true, validation required: true. Conditions: All translations must be validated by FehrAdvice. Semantic meaning is normatively binding, not literal form. Deviating semantic fields lead to loss of conformity. Supported languages: German, English, French. Forbidden terms: rational, irrational, optimal, suboptimal, objective, subjective. Rationale: These terms are not permitted in BCM because they are semantically linked with normative value judgments and distort empirical model logic. Domain limit: Valid domains: Behavioral Economics, Decision Theory, Social Psychology, Organizational Research, Governance Design. Excluded domains: Theology, Pure Philosophy, Ideological Discourses, Non-empirical Cultural Theories. Rationale: Meta-axioms apply exclusively in empirically verifiable, systems-theoretically mappable domains. Integration with other axioms: References: A5, A6, A10. Description: A7 is directly linked with A5 (Functional Principle), A6 (Coherence), and A10 (Governance) to ensure linguistic, logical, and ethical consistency. Watchdog binding: Component: BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Check type: linguistic_integrity_check. Check frequency: monthly. Error code: E7-LINGUISTIC-DRIFT. Response: Soft Warning – Recommendation for semantic validation. Governance binding: Supervised by FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Review cycle: annually. Approval required for new languages: true. License requirement: FehrAdvice Translation & Validation License. Audit reference: meta_linguistic_integrity_9251. Meta linguistic engine: Component: BEATRIX Kernel Linguistic Parser. Function: Detection and correction of semantic drift. Mechanisms: Detection of semantically prohibited terms, Mapping of meaning levels via BCM thesaurus, Self-healing for translation deviations. Self-healing: enabled: true, Mechanism: Automatic reinterpretation based on base language (German). Version: 3.0.2025. Status: active. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Contributors: Gerhard Fehr, Andrea Fehr, BEATRIX Kernel Development Team. Approval date: 2025-10-31.

A8.title: Versioning and Validity
A8.text: This chapter defines the versioning logic, compatibility guidelines, and audit mechanisms for meta-axioms (MA 0.00–0.99). It ensures that all system components use the same meta-axiom base and that changes remain transparent, reversible, and traceable. Version model: Current version: 3.0.2025. Previous version: 2.5.2024. Next planned version: 3.1.2026. Version policy: Major change (New axiom families or structural rules e.g., MA_0.40), Minor change (Extension of existing rules without changing basic structure), Patch change (Bug fixing or semantic correction). Semantic versioning: true. Backward compatibility: enabled: true, Mechanism: Legacy Axiom Handler (BCM3_01_WATCHDOG), Description: Older modules (≤ v2.x) remain compatible as their meta-axioms are automatically mapped to current semantics. Change log: Version 3.0.2025 - Introduction of Axiom MA_0.40 (Lexical Identity), Extension of A5–A7 to operational meta-architecture, Link to governance audit (A10), Approved by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board, Approval date: 2025-10-31. Version 2.5.2024 - Integration of context obligation (MA_0.26) and declaration obligation (MA_0.31), Integration of standard BCM2_10_STD10061, Approved by FehrAdvice R&D Zürich, Approval date: 2024-07-12. Distribution policy: Propagation: automatic via kernel (9249). Trigger modules: BCM3_00_INIT9249_KERNEL, BCM3_01_WATCHDOG, BCM2_10_STD10061. Update mechanism: Method: rolling update, Fallback: rollback to last stable version, Audit trigger: every versioning increase ≥ minor. Validation protocol: Supervised by BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Check frequency: monthly. Audit type: meta_version_consistency. Auto sync: true. Auto sync description: Kernel automatically synchronizes meta-versions between modules and enforces consistency. Governance binding: Supervised by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Approval required for major changes: true. Ethics review by FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Audit reference: meta_version_governance_9251. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Maintainer: BEATRIX Kernel Core Team. Location: Zürich, Switzerland. Review date: 2025-10-31. Status: active. Version: 3.0.2025.

A9.title: Citation and References
A9.text: This chapter defines the citation, reference, and validation standards for meta-axioms, modules, and scientific sources within the BCM and BEATRIX architecture. It ensures that every derivation, analysis, and simulation can be traced back to verifiable, audited sources. Citation model: Citation standard: APA 7th Edition (FehrAdvice Extended Schema). Reference prefix: FA-REF. Example: FehrAdvice & Partners AG (2025). BCM2_00_META7232. Zürich. Machine readable format: JSON-LD (Linked Data). Validation: Required fields: author, year, title, module_reference, source_type. Auto validation: true. Validation engine: BCM3_01_WATCHDOG. Error code: E9-CITATION-INCONSISTENCY. Reference integrity: Source types: Primary Source (API content, FehrAdvice original modules), Secondary Source (peer-reviewed scientific papers), Tertiary Source (meta-analyses or systematic reviews). Hierarchy: Primary > Secondary > Tertiary. Description: Only primary sources may directly justify meta-axioms. Secondary and tertiary sources serve contextualization. Cross-reference: Module linking: true. Mechanism: CrossRef-ID + chapter_content_id. Example: BCM2_05_AWX[7240]:FA-REF-2025-07. Integrity check: Run frequency: monthly, Component: BCM3_01_WATCHDOG, Check type: reference_consistency_check. Citation audit protocol: Audited by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Audit frequency: quarterly. Audit scope: Existence check (sources present?), Integrity check (sources unchanged?), Coherence check (citation logic consistent?). Auto correction: enabled: true, Method: Automatic reloading from API sources (my.fehradvice.com), Fallback: local reference library. Report format: FA_CIT_AUDIT_REPORT_9251.json. Governance binding: Supervised by FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Ethics binding: FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Approval required for external sources: true. License requirement: FehrAdvice Research & Citation License. Audit reference: meta_citation_integrity_9251. Integration with other axioms: References: A5, A8, A10. Description: A9 directly interacts with A5 (Functional Principle), A8 (Versioning), and A10 (Governance) to ensure citations remain consistent across time, source, and responsibility. Author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG. Contributors: Gerhard Fehr, Andrea Fehr, BEATRIX Kernel Development Team. Approval date: 2025-10-31. Status: active. Version: 3.0.2025.

A10.title: License and Ownership
A10.text: This chapter defines the ethical, legal, and organizational principles for the control, ownership, application, and monitoring of meta-axioms (MA 0.00–0.99). It ensures that scientific integrity, transparency, and accountability are maintained at all system levels. Governance structure: Scientific board: Name: FehrAdvice Scientific Advisory Board. Role: Scientific supervision of the development and application of all axioms. Composition: Independent researchers and senior advisors with expertise in Behavioral Economics and Decision Theory. Approval rights: Introduction of new meta-axioms, Changes to core modules (A5–A9), Release of versioning (A8). Ethics council: Name: FehrAdvice Ethics & Integrity Council. Role: Reviews ethical, communicative, and societal impacts of model applications. Functions: Approval of intervention architectures, Assessment of potential usage conflicts, Publication of annual Ethics Impact Reports. Operational responsibility: Owner: FehrAdvice & Partners AG, Zürich. Maintainer: BEATRIX Kernel Development Team. License manager: FehrAdvice IP & Legal Unit.
